severity_definition.severe: New relative-to-initial global person/identity/body collapse or major unusable structural defect.
severity_definition.moderate: New visible localized head direction, expression, face clarity or hand-position/clarity loss while subject and overall body remain recognizable.
severity_definition.none: No clear moderate/severe new regression. Improved labels describe a visible local benefit, not complete target compliance.

moderate_new_regressions.reason: J turns the head toward camera and downward; initial was nearer B strong side profile. Clear new head-direction regression.
J face is blurrier/flatter around glasses, nose and lips than the initial output; confidence is lower because source Face geometry is invalid.
Both retain A open smile instead of B rounded-mouth expression. The hand-position/clarity loss is new.
B looks toward camera; J gaze and mouth shape depart more. The face remains plausible, so this is localized.
J opens the mouth widely and furrows brows, producing a shout/grimace absent from B and initial.
Both entirely miss B chin-up/head-back pose; J open-mouth smile is an additional expression error compared with initial.
J wide laughing/shouting mouth is absent from closed-mouth B and exceeds initial slight mouth opening.
Both miss B side profile; J grin introduces a further expression mismatch versus the more neutral initial face.
J turns and lowers the head away from B frontal raised-chin pose, more than initial. A smile is copied instead of B mouth/neck pose.
J removes B/A open smile and produces a neutral/downturned mouth. This is an expression tradeoff, despite improved identity score.
J tips head downward/frontward; B and initial are more sideward and upright. Clear head-direction tradeoff.
J closes eyes and opens a large dark mouth absent from A, B and initial; clear unwanted expression.

conclusion: Legacy observation: TikTok24 remains letterbox-compatible, but iPER12 and pooled36 are superseded and must not inform the current letterbox36 final comparison. J256 preserves overall subject/body/scene and provides several local appearance gains. iPER identity and strict PCK improve on average, but head direction/expression remain unreliable. TikTok mean identity is flat with localized regressions. This observation does not modify the J_mid gate or claim Face control is achieved.
limitations: All labels are manual qualitative observations of actual saved images; no blinded human-rating study or significance claim.
TikTok covers only three original video groups; frames are correlated. iPER faces are small at native resolution.
ArcFace measures similarity to A and PCK measures sparse body/head joints; neither establishes B expression or exact head yaw/pitch success.
Source glasses/accessories are often retained while B changes their position; source identity and target expression can trade off.
Missing identity is not imputed; this specific comparison has36/36 unique source/output detections in both runs.
TikTok index9 has invalid source Face geometry/condition and no source Face crop in both runs; whole A was reviewed and the fixed B output crop remains available.

body_face_ablation_diagnostic.scope: Four exact same TikTok indices0,7,14,22, with same J256 checkpoint/seed42/30steps/512px. Extra eight ablation outputs, plus four existing common J outputs. Kept outside primary36 visual counts/metric denominators.
body_face_ablation_diagnostic.conclusion: Actual images show FaceOnly largely reproduces A source pose/composition in all four cases, rather than successful B redirection. Its high ArcFace reflects source retention. BodyPlusFace and BodyOnly have nearly identical broad poses and identical per-case PCK; BodyPlusFace has only a small same-four identity mean increase. This limited diagnostic does not establish statistical effects, all-cohort superiority or that Face is unnecessary.
interpretation_limits: FaceOnly removes Body geometry entirely; source preservation may arise from the underlying image-editing pipeline as well as Face features. This is a diagnostic, not causal attribution to Face alone.
MAE is a pixel correspondence check within the actual valid image rectangle, used to support the visually observed source composition retention; it is not an identity or perceptual quality metric.
A fixed B crop may contain sky when the generated face stays at A location; that is not a full-image face-detector failure.
No comparison of these4-case means to the full36 cohort averages is made.

cases.observation: FaceOnly retains A strong side profile, hair fall and forward-lean composition instead of B more frontal head turn. BodyOnly and Body+Face follow the broad target composition, with similarly approximate head direction.
FaceOnly keeps both A arms over the head and A front-facing expression; B arms are lowered in front with a sideward closed-mouth head. BodyOnly and Body+Face lower the arms toward B.

FaceOnly keeps A forward/side bend, lowered gaze/closed eyes and leftward arm sweep; it does not adopt B camera-facing raised near arm. BodyOnly and Body+Face adopt the broad B arm arrangement, though their gaze is imperfect.

FaceOnly preserves A outstretched arms and original face position, while B has bent elbows and downward side-turn/hair occlusion. Its fixed B target face crop contains sky because the output face stayed at A position; the full-image detector still finds one face. BodyOnly and Body+Face change the arm layout toward B.
